decisive_items: brownish macules on the hands and feet
hyperchromic punctate lesions on the trunk
numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum
response.rationale: R2 is the champion because it has the most comprehensive set of supporting evidence, including mucocutaneous melanin deposits and gastrointestinal polyps, which are characteristic of Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome. R5 is the runner-up because it also has a strong set of supporting evidence, including chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, and weight loss, which are consistent with Crohn's Disease. However, R2 has a more distinctive set of features that are less common in other conditions.

rejected.why: less specific symptoms and laboratory findings
symptoms and laboratory findings are not as distinctive as those of R2
